description: A new type of search system with pattern recognition. Enterprise-grade search in a class library.
releaseNotes:
Release candidate. Coverage ranking, which is on for every search by default: nine fixes and one
      change to how a query being typed is ranked. Scores change for many searches, and the order of
      results with them; nothing throws, and nothing stored needs converting. One case needs action: an
      engine using a two-way `TextNormalizer` should be rebuilt with `Index()`.
      
      - Fixed: a query containing a character the normalizer folds, such as "blåbær" with the default
        normalizer, now gets full coverage against a document containing the same word. The document text
        was folded and the query words were not, so the two never met and the document scored about two
        thirds of what it should.
      - Fixed: a document's coverage score no longer depends on which other documents the search met
        first. The first document whose text folded rewrote the query for every document after it.
      - Fixed: word order is judged relatively. A query's words in order anywhere in a document count as
        in order; before, only words at the same position as in the query did, so "blue straw" in
        "big blue straw hat" scored as if the words were swapped. A word out of order now costs 257, the
        same everywhere; below full coverage it had cost a share of the score that could outweigh
        covering more of the query.
      - Fixed: a document covering the whole query with words out of order no longer ties with one that
        has them in order when a joined or near-miss word completes the match.
      - Fixed: one word in a document can no longer be credited for two query words by the edit-distance
        matching, and every query word matched as a prefix or suffix now counts towards truncation, where
        at most one had.
      - Fixed: with a two-way `TextNormalizer` (`oneWayMode: false`) the query is now folded before
        scoring, so "blåbær" and "blabar" are the same search, as two-way means. The query had been
        scored with its characters unfolded against an index that holds only folded ones. The index also
        held unfolded copies of words, so a document and its folded twin scored differently; rebuild with
        `Index()` to drop them. The default normalizer is one-way and is not affected.
      - Changed: when the whole query appears in a document as one string, the document scores at least
        65535 if it starts the document, 65519 if it starts a word further in, 8 less for either if it
        ends inside a word, and (q − 1) / q of the maximum if it starts inside a word, q being the query
        length. This is what ranks a query being typed: for "knut h" the "h" is too short to count as a
        word, so "knut hamsun" and "knut faldbakken" used to score alike. Before, the whole-query match
        counted only when no word matched at all. Turn it off with `CoverageSetup.CoverWholeQuery`.
      - Changed: a document that does not begin with the query's first word scores 16 less than one that
        does, so among equal matches the one starting with the query still ranks first.
title: IndxSearchLib
